title: Two calendar events clash and the priority rules cannot settle it
when: Two events land at the same time and neither outranks the other (for example two showings of two listings at 2 pm).
steps: Agent 18 (Calendar & Task Management) keeps the first event on the calendar.
It does not put the second one on; it asks you to decide.
It never moves either event on its own.
never: Silently move or drop either event.
why: Which appointment gives way is a judgment about clients and relationships. That is yours.
you_see: A question about the conflict at that time.
test: Buyer B1 asks to see listing L1 at 2 pm on October 20; buyer B2 asks to see L2 at the same time. Open finding: Agent 06 (Showing Scheduler) still sends B2 a showing confirmation, because it never hears the calendar's answer. The buyer is told "confirmed" while you are asked to decide.

title: A briefing item has no source on record
when: Something in the morning briefing points to a message that is not on the record.
steps: The briefing lists it as a gap, naming the missing source.
Items that rest on real messages are not listed as gaps.
never: Present an item whose source is missing as if it were sound.
why: A briefing item with no record behind it cannot be checked. Saying so keeps the briefing honest.
you_see: A gap listed in the briefing.
test: The test plants a waiting item (an inspection report) whose source message is not on the record, then asks for the briefing.

title: Your instruction conflicts with a contract deadline
when: You ask for something to be scheduled at a time that conflicts with a contract deadline (for example a final walkthrough after closing).
steps: Agent 18 holds it and shows you both: your instruction and the deadline.
Nothing is scheduled until you decide. Continue goes ahead; cancel drops the instruction.
An instruction with no conflict goes straight on the calendar.
never: Act on either the instruction or the deadline before you decide.
why: A walkthrough after closing is likely a mistake; the system asks rather than guessing which date you meant.
you_see: A held instruction showing the conflict, asking you to continue or cancel.
test: Closing is October 22. You ask for the final walkthrough on October 25: held; you cancel and it is dropped. On another transaction a walkthrough before closing goes on the calendar.

title: An agent asks to move a protected deadline block
when: An agent asks to move a calendar block that protects a contract deadline.
steps: Only you can move it; it tells you the request was refused.
never: Move a deadline block at an agent's request.
why: Deadline blocks protect contract dates. Only your confirmation moves them.
you_see: A question saying the request to move the protected block was refused.
test: A closing deadline is on the calendar. You relay, as a signed setting, a request from Agent 06 to move it (agents have no route to ask this themselves).

title: A day is overbooked
when: A day has more events than the daily limit (8 in your settings).
steps: Agent 18 proposes an order of priority for the day.
never: Reorder or drop events on its own.
why: When everything cannot happen, you decide what comes first.
you_see: A question saying the day is at capacity, with a proposed order.
test: Nine showings are requested on one day; nine calendar requests reach Agent 18 and you are asked about the ninth. Open finding: the ninth buyer is still sent a showing confirmation by Agent 06.

title: Two sources give different dates for the same deadline
when: The transaction timeline and a document disagree on a deadline date.
steps: It tells you about the conflict, naming both sources.
The morning briefing lists the conflict.
why: Choosing the later date can make a deadline pass unnoticed. Both stay visible until you settle it.
you_see: A question about the conflicting dates; the conflict in the briefing.
test: The timeline says the inspection is due October 25; the inspection report says October 22.

title: Your calendar clashes with a contract deadline
when: A soft item on your calendar (for example a showing) falls on the day of a contract deadline.
steps: The deadline outranks the soft item.
Agent 18 proposes moving the soft item and asks you.
never: Move the deadline to fit the calendar.
why: Showings can move; closing dates cannot.
you_see: A question naming the deadline and the soft items that clash with it.
test: A showing at 10:00 on October 20; closing is also October 20.

title: A recurring task quietly stops happening
when: A task that should repeat shows no completions.
steps: Agent 18 reports the pattern to you.
never: Treat a quiet calendar as a sign that all is well.
why: A task that silently stopped is a problem nobody sees until it is too late.
you_see: A report about the silent task.

title: It is unclear which time zone a party is in
when: Someone involved may be in a different time zone and it has not been confirmed.
steps: Agent 18 confirms the time zone before scheduling.
why: A closing scheduled in the wrong time zone can miss its window.
you_see: A question confirming the time zone.
